geography: Ember country or economy rows, using its ISO 3 code. Regional aggregates remain in the original source download.

methodology.source: Ember, Yearly Electricity Data, 17 November 2026. Some recent figures use monthly reporting or estimates. Coverage varies by economy, source and year.
methodology.sources: The chart shows four fuel groups. The table also includes their components and broader totals. Renewables includes hydro, wind, solar, bioenergy and other renewables. Clean also includes nuclear. Ember publishes each value separately.
methodology.system: Generation and demand are annual quantities. Net imports can be negative. Installed capacity measures power in GW. The emissions series cover the lifecycle of domestic generation.
methodology.processing: Each history reads the indicated row and column from the global CSV. Blank and absent cells stay missing. Numeric zeros, signed trade and published group totals are preserved. Each country CSV retains the original decimal text. The release has no estimate flag per observation.

electricity-demand.name: Electricity demand
electricity-demand.definition: Electricity supplied to meet demand, including system losses. Ember calculates demand from domestic generation and net imports.

electricity-total-generation.name: Total domestic generation
electricity-total-generation.definition: Electricity generated domestically during the year. Ember aims to report gross generation and reconciles several national and international sources.

electricity-net-imports.name: Net electricity imports
electricity-net-imports.definition: Imports less exports. Negative values indicate net exports. Ember carries forward some trade estimates and assumes zero in some cases with unavailable trade statistics.

electricity-total-capacity.name: Total installed capacity
electricity-total-capacity.definition: Installed generating capacity measures the power that equipment can deliver. Annual electricity production is measured separately in TWh.

electricity-emissions.name: Power-generation emissions
electricity-emissions.definition: Estimated lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions from domestic electricity generation, expressed in million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent.

electricity-intensity.name: Emissions per unit of electricity generated
electricity-intensity.definition: Estimated lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions per kilowatt-hour generated domestically. Ember applies fuel-specific emission factors.
